fields.note: 70 words · live is 22 · the live note raises conformity requirements and explains nothing, which leaves the buyer with a worry and no answer. Saudi Arabia’s SABER platform, run by SASO, issues a product certificate and a per-shipment certificate, and no shipment clears without the second one. Naming the process and offering the documents is the single most useful thing this page can say to a Saudi buyer, and no competing Indian supplier page mentions SABER at all. Deliberately not claimed: that Margo holds a SABER certificate, or that these components sit in a regulated category — that is per-product and per-importer, and stating the process without claiming the outcome is the defensible version

notes: SABER is the term to own. SABER certificate rubber components and SASO conformity India supplier are searched by Saudi importers and Indian exporters alike, and no Indian rubber supplier page carries either. It is the export equivalent of the ISPM-15 note on the mining page.

Do not claim a SABER certificate. The certificate is held per product by the importer of record, category coverage changes, and the 2026 rules tightened the HS code and product declaration requirements. Describing the process and offering the technical file is the claim that stays true.

fields.label: Q1 — new, and it leads

lines: Do you hold NORSOK M-710 or API elastomer qualification?

parts.text: Not today. The qualification programme is under way and is targeted for 2027. Margo holds ISO 9001:2015, certificate 09111526A, and supplies hydrocarbon-service sealing against controlled drawing revisions with material certificates and batch records issued per shipment. Where your specification calls for NORSOK or API qualification, tell us at enquiry stage and we will confirm the current position on that programme before you commit engineering time.
parts.lead: The qualification programme is under way and is targeted for 2027.

fields.note: 72 words · new question, and it belongs first. It is the qualifying question in hydrocarbon service and the live page never raises it — four FAQ questions, none about certification, on a page written for oil and gas buyers. Silence is the worst of the three possible answers, because a buyer who cannot find the position assumes the least favourable one. The closing sentence is the same construction the automotive page uses for IATF: state the position, then say what happens next

fields.label: Q2 — new

parts.text: Margo Rubber Products holds ISO 9001:2015, certificate 09111526A, issued by Integral Certification Ltd and valid to 21 February 2027. We are actively upgrading our quality management system to IATF 16949:2016, with certification targeted by the end of 2026, and ISO 14001, ISO 45001 and NORSOK/API qualification targeted for 2027. Material test reports and batch certificates are issued with every shipment.

fields.note: 61 words · new question, carrying the canonical wording settled across the set. It must render from the same constant as the automotive, mining, about, products and certifications pages

fields.label: Q3

lines: What is the typical lead time for components shipped to the UAE?

parts.text: Three to four weeks ex-works Nashik from drawing approval, or two weeks on an express basis where we have confirmed capacity. A new component with tooling to cut adds the tooling lead time, quoted per part. Nhava Sheva to Jebel Ali runs a further five to nine days port to port — one of the shortest lanes out of India — with air freight quoted where a shutdown date requires it.
parts.lead: Three to four weeks ex-works Nashik from drawing approval

fields.note: 72 words · live is 37 · the live answer is wrong twice and stops short once. 14–21 and 21–35 days against the 3–4 weeks published everywhere else; and it ends on “before sea freight transit to Jebel Ali” without the figure. The transit number is a selling point on this lane, not a caveat — five to nine days is faster than almost any alternative origin and the live page declines to say so

fields.label: Q4

lines: Which compounds do you recommend for hydrocarbon service?

parts.text: FKM is the usual choice where petroleum oils, fuels or solvents are present at sustained temperature, rated to +250 °C. NBR suits moderate-temperature oil contact to +120 °C. EPDM is specified for water, steam and desalination duty but must not be used in petroleum service. Send your media, service temperature and pressure class and we will confirm the compound and hardness.

fields.note: 62 words · live is 40 · the live answer is correct and gains three figures plus one warning. The EPDM exclusion is the addition that prevents a failure — EPDM is the compound most often mis-specified into oil service, and on a hydrocarbon page saying so is worth more than another capability claim

fields.label: Q5

lines: Can you supply against our own drawings and standards?

parts.text: Yes. Components are produced against your controlled drawing revision, with no substitutions without approval. Standards are named by number on the documentation — AS568, ISO 3601, JIS B2401 and DIN 3771 for O-rings; ASME B16.21, EN 1514-1 and JIS B2404 for flange gaskets.

fields.note: 48 words · live is 26 · the live answer says “standards are named by number” and then names none. Listing the seven turns a promise into evidence, and every one is on a product sheet in this set

fields.label: Q6

lines: Do you provide material certificates with shipments?

parts.text: Yes. Raw material certificates and batch records are retained and issued per shipment, together with the inspection release data for the despatch lot. For Saudi consignments we also supply the technical file your conformity body needs for the SABER submission.
parts.lead: For Saudi consignments we also supply the technical file your conformity body needs for the SABER submission.

fields.note: 41 words · live is truncated in capture · the closing sentence connects the FAQ to the conformity process named in section 07, which is where a Saudi buyer’s next question goes

notes: Crawlability. All six answers in the DOM at first paint, collapsed with CSS.

Q1 is the most important answer on this page and it does not currently exist. “Is Margo NORSOK qualified?” is the question that decides whether a process engineer proceeds, and the site answers it on three pages a hydrocarbon buyer will not read.
Q3 is the compound question an assistant is asked — production lead time plus freight transit, from India to the Gulf, in one answer. Almost no supplier page provides both.

The EPDM exclusion in Q4 is a trust signal. Telling a buyer which of your own compounds not to use is the same move as the mining page’s wear-liner answer, and it is what makes the recommendations credible.
Question headings are <h3>, each a literal buyer question. Six Question children in the FAQPage node, answer text matching the visible copy word for word.
